Limits are the admission envelope of those individually checked modes on one head, not measured throughput or reserved bandwidth. Each job and rollback requires a fresh matching receipt, including receiver_mode_id=0 boot restoration.
mode_product_checkpoint.identity: Full common backend/output generation, ticket, sequence, operation and exact published timing/assignment/borrowed reference are checked. SYSTEM buffer must be tight linear XRGB8888 with required usage. The common reference remains borrowed. Original creator reference closes only after acknowledged handoff; retained display Use identifies its native allocation thereafter.
mode_product_checkpoint.apply: Actual RM allocation and individually acknowledged RAMHT update precede SYSTEM import, CE upload and coupled WIMM/Window/Core/final-HDMI commit. Only real runtime completion selects candidate Present slot and sends applied/quiesced=1. Previous slot remains held pending a common decision.
mode_product_checkpoint.decision: The common kernel owner controls confirmation deadlines. Confirm retires the old SYSTEM mapping/import, RAMHT and native allocation before receipt. Rollback reconstructs and freshly checks the saved mode, commits/selects the old image, then retires candidate completely before old_preserved/quiesced=2. Borrowed reference is never closed by NVIDIA.
mode_product_checkpoint.failure: Known pre-allocation rejection preserves old state and reports unsupported/timeout. Uncertain submitted effects report lost/quiesced=0; first phase/error and actual owners remain held. Recovery is not optimistically acknowledged. Fully restoring the original firmware/boot mapping is still open.
mode_product_checkpoint.diagnostics: native-modes logs ready, begin, complete or failed-held with exact ticket/sequence/operation, phase, old/new image names, outcome and common completion status. Existing runtime records carry source/IMP, CE/display points and resource retirement. Complete coherent before/after/restore diagnosis remains open.
